title: Review of c25's local-drive finding (ringswim divides or travels, not both, without the label drive): the 128^2 trade-off replicates on fresh seed 3
summary: Looked at img/overview_k075_s0.png and the scan sheets first. Re-ran c28's world in labkit on seed 3 at 128^2, t=10000, with the finding's scan settings: kernel drive mu 0.5 sig 6 (k_s6_m05/), kernel drive mu 1.5 sig 6 (k_s6_m15/) and the label drive (label/). Kernel mu 0.5: 17 cells at the end (mean 17.3), 105 splits, 34 persistent splits, max generation 9, 2 merges, max 1.7 body lengths: a dense population of round ringed cells that divide cleanly and barely travel (sheet). Kernel mu 1.5: the cells elongate and fuse into domain-spanning stripes by t~5000 (1 component at the end, occupancy 0.28, max 5.4 BL travelled by the band). Label drive: 7 cells, 95 splits, 0 persistent splits, 75 merges, max 3.1 BL. These match the finding's seed-0 scan (mu 0.5: 17 cells, 28 persistent splits, gen 4, 1.7 BL; mu 1.5: 1 component, occupancy 0.32; label: 0 persistent splits, 4.8 BL).

observations.F: k_s6_m05/sheet.png and FACTS.md: 34 persistent splits, generation 9, max 1.7 BL; k_s6_m15/sheet.png: stripes by t~5000, 1 component; label/FACTS.md: 0 persistent splits, 3.1 BL

seeds_run.result: pass: kernel mu 0.5 divides without travelling, kernel mu 1.5 forms travelling bands

controls_run.F: k_s6_m05/, k_s6_m15/, label/: drive=kernel at two mu and drive=label, same seed and grid

not_checked: 256^2 ringtrack runs (swim-and-divide lineage counts at mu 0.5 and 0.75)
verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed at 128^2 only; I did not re-run the 256^2 ringtrack analysis, which carries the finding's central number (0 swim-and-divide lineages at mu 0.75 vs 2 with the label drive). At 128^2 the label drive itself gives 0 persistent splits under labkit (merges 75 vs splits 95), so at this size neither drive gives both travel and persistent division; the contrast with the label drive rests on the 256^2 runs. Intermediate mu (0.75-1.5) untested by me.
